claims.text: Retracement falls monotonically down the chain: gas, then crude, then resin, then finished product.
claims.source: FRED/BLS and EIA monthly series, each indexed to January 2019; retracement = (peak - now) / (peak - 100)
claims.assert: (lambda g: g['feedstock'] > g['resin'] > g['product'])({s['stage']: max(x['retraced'] for x in D['series'] if x['stage']==s['stage'] and x['retraced'] is not None) for s in D['series'] if s['stage'] in ('feedstock','resin','product')})
claims.actual: [(s['stage'], s['label'], s['retraced']) for s in D['series'] if s['retraced'] is not None]
claims.falsified_if: Any stage overtakes the one above it. The ORDERING is the claim and it is robust to the base month; the exact percentages are not, because January 2019 is a winter month and flatters the gas fall.

claims.text: Finished polymer product prices have retraced nothing — their peak is the most recent month.
claims.source: PPI plastics and rubber products manufacturing, PCU326326
claims.assert: all(s['retraced'] == 0 and s['peak']['date'] == s['now']['date'] for s in D['series'] if s['stage']=='product')
claims.actual: [(s['label'], s['peak']['date'], s['peak']['index'], s['now']['index']) for s in D['series'] if s['stage']=='product']
claims.falsified_if: Any month prints below the prior peak — at which point this page's headline is out of date and must be restated. This is the most perishable claim on the site; it expires with the next PPI release.

claims.text: Natural gas is below where it started in January 2019.
claims.assert: (lambda g: g['now']['index'] < 100 and g['retraced'] > 1)([s for s in D['series'] if 'natural gas' in s['label'].lower()][0])
claims.actual: [(s['label'], s['peak']['index'], s['now']['index'], s['retraced']) for s in D['series'] if 'natural gas' in s['label'].lower()]
claims.falsified_if: Gas rises back above its January 2019 level. Note the base is a WINTER month, so this comparison is flattering by construction — the honest version is that gas has fully round-tripped, not that it is cheap.

claims.text: The product-minus-resin spread is stated as an index spread and never as a margin.
claims.source: Standing rule - labor, freight, energy and packaging are in neither index
claims.falsified_if: Anyone describes this line as profit, margin, or markup. Two readings fit the same line - the industry held price after input costs fell, or its other costs rose enough to require it - and this data cannot separate them.
claims.checked_by: Unit-discipline rule, not a data check

claims.text: Series in different units share an axis only because every one is rebased to its own January 2019.
claims.source: derive_rest.py indexes each series to its base month before any chart sees it
claims.assert: all(s['base'] == '2019-01-01' for s in D['series']) and 'rebasing' in D['meta']
claims.falsified_if: Any raw level reaches a shared axis. Dollars per mcf, cents per kWh and index points are not comparable quantities, and indexing is the only thing that makes one axis honest here.
